missing_diagram_candidates.description: The long text-only counterexample defines a delicate multiscale mesh: mirrored alternating-radius root fans in a pentagonal domain, repeated attachment triples, recursively nested child holes with a strict seven-node boundary, protected fan/crease relations, and conforming collar/guard transitions. A compact three-panel schematic would clarify the global fan and mirrored attachment sites, one seven-node child and protected holes, and the root-to-existing-top-right pressure crease plus common uniform cutoff ring.
diagram_relations: root o to consecutive alternating-radius fan vertices v_j and v_(j+1), mirrored across vertical axis
equally spaced attachment triples on middle thirds of long fan sides; child radius proportional to spacing
child boundary has exactly seven prescribed nodes; no subdivision of child top edge
crease from existing root to existing top-right corner; stays outside protected fan cones and recursive holes
cutoff varies only on common uniform annulus outside child transition
missing_diagram_candidates.caveat: Editorial aid only: no image is claimed missing as a rendering defect; source gives explicit geometry but its scale and nested relations are hard to retain in prose.
